# Scanpath Studio

> Free, open-source software for visualizing eye-tracking data from reading studies: scanpaths, fixations, saccades, gaze heatmaps and raw gaze drawn over the text, from EyeLink, Tobii and other eye trackers.

Scanpath Studio is an interactive Streamlit workbench, a Python API (`import scanpath_studio as sps`) and a CLI (`scanpath-studio`) for eye-tracking-while-reading data: it draws fixations, saccades and heatmaps over the text at its true on-screen position, shows the per-word reading measures your data brings (FFD, FPRT, RPD, TFD, skips, regressions), compares participants, and exports figures and tables. The bundled demo is a subset of the OneStop Eye Movements corpus.

# Use the app

# Get started

## Install

- **Desktop app** Recommended

  No coding required. Your data stays on your computer.

  [macOS](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/releases/latest/download/ScanpathStudio-macos-arm64.dmg) [Windows](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/releases/latest/download/ScanpathStudio-windows-x86_64-setup.exe) [Linux](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/releases/latest/download/ScanpathStudio-linux-x86_64.tar.gz)

  Setup details & other downloads

  - macOS 14+, Apple silicon: open the DMG, drag to Applications, then launch. If blocked: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. Intel Mac or older macOS? Use Python below.
  - Windows: run the installer, then launch from Start. If SmartScreen warns: More info → Run anyway. A [portable ZIP](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/releases/latest/download/ScanpathStudio-windows-x86_64.zip) is also available.
  - Linux: extract, then run `./ScanpathStudio/ScanpathStudio`.

  [All downloads](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/releases/latest)

- **Try online**

  Explore the bundled demo without installing anything.

  [Launch demo](https://scanpath-studio-dev.streamlit.app)

- **Install with Python**

  Requires Python 3.11–3.15. Runs on your computer and opens in your browser.

  ```
  pip install scanpath-studio
  scanpath-studio
  ```

## Try the Dev build

Stable is the published release on PyPI and the desktop downloads above. Dev follows the changes merged into `main`. You can [open the Dev app](https://scanpath-studio-dev.streamlit.app) or run it locally. In a separate Python environment with Git installed, run:

```
python -m pip install "git+https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio.git@dev"
scanpath-studio
```

**Help** shows which channel you are running. Its release notes are in **About & citation → App details**.

For a Git installation, the update command keeps your repository, requested ref and package subdirectory. An install from an official release tag follows the Stable channel for updates. If you selected a commit hash, choose the new revision in your original install command when you are ready to move.

## Replay a sample reading

On your first visit, the app opens a reading from the [OneStop demo](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/loading-data/#onestop). Choose **Replay this reading** to follow the reader’s fixations over the text. Press **Pause**, then **Next fixation** to step through the recording. You can return to the sample walkthrough from **Help → Task guides**.

To work with your own recording, choose **Import my data** or follow [Add your own data](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/loading-data/#add-your-own-data).

## Your first figure

Choose a reading in the demo to explore and save as an interactive figure.

\[!\[

\](../assets/workflows/design-presets_poster.webp)\](../assets/workflows/design-presets.mp4)

- **1 · Open a reading**

  In the **Scanpath View**, choose **Bundled demo** in **Select dataset**. Then choose a reading in **Select trial**.

- **2 · Choose a view**

  Choose **Heatmap** to see where fixation time concentrates, or **Scanpath** to follow the order of fixations. Both tiles sit under **Presets** in Essentials and Full.

- **3 · Save your figure**

  In the **Export** tab under the plot, find **Current figure**. Set **Download format** to **HTML**, then click **⬇ Download HTML**. Open the saved file in your browser to zoom and hover over the figure.

# Analyze a corpus

- **[Analyze one text](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/corpus-analysis/analyze-one-text/index.md)**

  Compare word-by-word measures across participants.

- **[Compare groups or conditions](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/corpus-analysis/compare-groups/index.md)**

  Inspect group means and differences.

- **[Track changes over time](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/corpus-analysis/progression-over-time/index.md)**

  Inspect trends within or across trials.

## Before you start

Open a dataset and set the trial filters for your question. Word-level views need [reading measures in the Words table](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/loading-data/#reading-measures); the bundled demo includes them. To compare participants on one text, their trials of that text must share one text ID.

Choose **Texts** to compare passages or **Participants** to compare readers. Select a dot to see its mean, range and how many readings contributed. **Open word profile** shows where in a text the values change. **Open participant profile** compares one reader’s word values with the others.

## Keep the result

Open **Table and downloads** under a text or participant comparison. In a detailed analysis that produces a table, use **Download results**. The CSV saves the values. **Download recipe (JSON)** saves the dataset name, the trial filters, the analysis choices and the counts. Keep the source data alongside the recipe so you can reproduce the result.

To draw a summary with Python or the CLI, see [Plot a summary in code](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/corpus-workspace/#plot-a-summary-in-code).

# Analyze one text

1. [Select the trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/corpus-analysis/#before-you-start), then open **Corpus Analysis** and choose a **Reading measure**. In the bundled demo, try **Total fixation duration — TFD**.
1. In **Texts**, select a dot or use **Find a text**, then choose **Open word profile**. The **Cohort profile** shows a point for each word with enough observations. Hover over a point to read the word and its value.
1. Open **Readings behind a word** to check which participants supplied a value. A blank cell means that reading had no recorded value for the selected measure. In **Chart settings**, **Aggregate** sets how the profile combines values, **Spread** controls the shaded band, and **Min participants per word** sets how many readers must contribute.
1. In **Chart settings**, use **View** to explore the same text. **Measure on the stimulus** colors the words in their original positions. **Measure vs feature** compares the reading measure with a feature in the Words table, such as surprisal.
1. [Download the table and recipe](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/corpus-analysis/#keep-the-result).

If your data has no mapped **Text ID**, open **Texts** to inspect a single reading by its trial ID. To compare several readings, map the Words column that identifies the same passage across participants. If the page asks for reading measures, **Map reading measures** opens the column mapping for an editable dataset. For an upload that contains only fixations or gaze samples, **Add a Words table** opens the editor where you can attach the report.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/corpus-analysis_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/corpus-analysis.mp4)

*The recording shows total fixation duration on a text, against GPT-2 surprisal, and between two groups.*

# Compare groups or conditions

To compare two reading conditions in the bundled demo, use the advanced (**Adv**) and elementary (**Ele**) versions of its texts.

1. [Select the trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/corpus-analysis/#before-you-start), then open **Corpus Analysis** and select **Groups**. Choose a measure.
1. In **Edit groups**, use **Split a field** and choose `difficulty_level`. Select **Adv** for Group A and **Ele** for Group B. Each group needs at least one value. To choose participants, texts or conditions separately for each group, use **Independent filter sets**. A group with no filters includes all selected trials.
1. Read **Difference (A − B)**. For total fixation duration, a difference of 20 ms means that Group A spent 20 ms longer per word on average. The counts show how many participants contributed a value to each mean. For a rate, a change from 30% in B to 40% in A is a difference of 10 percentage points.
1. [Download the table and recipe](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/corpus-analysis/#keep-the-result).

For a different comparison, open **Chart settings** and choose a **View**. To explore Group A on its own, turn off **Compare two groups**.

For each participant, **Group means & difference** averages the words with a recorded value across all their selected trials. A trial with more measured words has more weight in that participant's mean. The group mean then gives each participant equal weight. In **Participants**, each reading contributes one mean to the summary, so the two views can give different values.

A participant who read both conditions contributes to both group means. The **Standardized difference** (Cohen's d) is available only for groups with no participants in common.

# Track changes over time

Inspect a measure within trials or across a session.

1. [Select the trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/corpus-analysis/#before-you-start) and open **Corpus Analysis**.

1. To follow one reader, choose **Participants**, select a reader and open their profile. To follow a group, choose **Groups** and turn off **Compare two groups**. In **Chart settings**, choose the **View** you need.

   | Scope                                                       | View                            |
   | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
   | One participant across trials                               | **Per-trial trend**             |
   | Fixation duration within trials, pooled for one participant | **Fixation duration over time** |
   | A group across trials                                       | **Group trend**                 |

1. Choose a measure, and an **Aggregate** where the view offers one. Across-trial trends order each participant's trials by a `trial_index` or `TRIAL_INDEX` column. Without one, the app orders them by fixation time, or as listed, and this may differ from the order the trials were shown. For the within-trial view, set **X axis** to **Fixation order**, or to **Time (ms)** when the data records fixation onsets.

1. [Download the table and recipe](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/corpus-analysis/#keep-the-result).

  Review recordings of the same text.

- **[Review an experimenter's sessions](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/data-collection/audit-an-experimenter/index.md)**

  Review sessions by who collected them.

# Review an experimenter's sessions

Review recordings collected by one experimenter.

Before you start, switch to **Full** at the top of the **Scanpath View** ([Essentials and Full](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/#essentials-and-full)).

1. Keep the experimenter column when you import the data, under **Extra fields to keep**. If each participant had one experimenter, you can instead attach it in a participant metadata table.
1. Open the filter () beside **Select trial** and choose the experimenter. Columns of a participant metadata table are under **By participant**.
1. [Inspect and replay their trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/data-collection/check-a-session/#2-inspect-a-trial).
1. In **Annotations**, tag trials `review` and note recurring problems.
1. [Export the review](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/data-collection/check-a-session/#5-save-the-review).

To compare experimenters, turn on **Compare**. Use the filter on each scanpath's row to pick a different experimenter, and choose readings of the same text.

# Check a session

Inspect a recording and save the trials that need attention.

Before you start, switch to **Full** at the top of the **Scanpath View** ([Essentials and Full](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/#essentials-and-full)).

## 1. Open the session

[Import your tables](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/loading-data/#add-your-own-data), or select a loaded dataset. Check that its **Recording setup** matches the screen used in the experiment.

## 2. Inspect a trial

In the **Scanpath View**, pick a trial in **Select trial**. Turn on **Word boxes** and check:

- whether the boxes match the stimulus image, if you have one;
- where the fixations sit relative to the words;
- unexpected gaps, shifts or off-screen positions.

For a consistent offset, check [coordinate units and screen setup](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/faq/#the-fixations-dont-line-up-with-the-text).

## 3. Replay the recording

Choose **Animation** to follow the fixation order and timing. To mark short or long fixations, or fixations outside the text, open **Filters & highlights** ▾ → **Fixations** and set **Short**, **Long** or **Outside the text** to **Highlight**. A gap or an unusual scanpath does not tell you its cause.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/replay_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/replay.mp4)

## 4. Record the review

In **Annotations**, tag the trial `review` and write what you observed in **Notes**. Use ◀ ▶ beside **Select trial** to move through the session.

## 5. Save the review

Export favorites, tags and notes from **Data Management** → **Current dataset → Annotations → Export**. The file includes participant and trial IDs. **Open** on an annotation row returns to that trial.

To reconcile a second reviewer's notes, choose **Import**. The preview counts new, identical and differing entries. **Open disputed reading** displays both entries beside the scanpath for that reading. You can download the differences for discussion. **Apply import** adds new entries and keeps the current version of a differing note unless you select the replacement option.

For exclusion decisions, follow [Exclude unsuitable trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/data-filtering/exclude-unsuitable-trials/index.md).

# Compare two eye trackers

Review the same text recorded with two trackers or setups.

Before you start, switch to **Full** at the top of the **Scanpath View** ([Essentials and Full](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/#essentials-and-full)).

1. [Import each recording](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/loading-data/#add-your-own-data) as a separate dataset, each with the **Recording setup** of its tracker.
1. Open the first dataset in the **Scanpath View** and pick a trial.
1. Turn on **Compare**. In scanpath B's row, choose the second dataset in **Dataset B** and a trial of the same text in **Trial B**.
1. Compare fixation placement, spread and missing stretches. An overlay needs both datasets recorded on the same screen size. Otherwise the app shows the two scanpaths side by side.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/compare_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/compare.mp4)

*This recording compares two participants in the bundled demo. For two trackers, choose the second recording in **Dataset B**.*

Use [the session-review steps](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/data-collection/check-a-session/#4-record-the-review) to save observations.

# Filter data

- **[Exclude unsuitable trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/data-filtering/exclude-unsuitable-trials/index.md)**

  Leave tagged trials out.

- **[Select participants by a field](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/data-filtering/select-participants/index.md)**

  Use participant metadata.

- **[Find trials with specific fixation patterns](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/data-filtering/find-trials-for-an-analysis/index.md)**

  Select trials after inspecting fixations.

## Before you start

Open a dataset in the **Scanpath View**. The filter () beside **Select trial** selects whole trials. **Filters & highlights** in the Plot controls changes which fixations and saccades the figure draws. Switch to **Full** at the top of the Scanpath View to use trial filters, fixation highlights, and batch export ([Essentials and Full](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/#essentials-and-full)).

\[!\[

\](../../assets/workflows/trial-filtering_poster.webp)\](../../assets/workflows/trial-filtering.mp4)

## Check and export the selection

1. Check the remaining trial and participant counts and inspect a few trials.
1. Follow [Export every trial](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/exporting-figures/export-every-trial/index.md) and choose **All filtered trials**. The bundle's `index.csv` lists its files with their participant and trial IDs.
1. Keep a full decision record with [Data Management → Annotations → Export](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/data-collection/check-a-session/#5-save-the-review). The annotations in a bundle cover only the exported trials.

# Exclude unsuitable trials

Apply your exclusion criteria and leave rejected trials out of the selection.

Before you start, switch to **Full** at the top of the **Scanpath View** ([Essentials and Full](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/#essentials-and-full)).

1. [Review the session](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/data-collection/check-a-session/#2-inspect-a-trial). Judge each trial against your study's criteria. A scanpath pattern alone does not establish skimming or poor calibration.
1. In **Annotations**, tag rejected trials `exclude` and write a short reason in **Notes**.
1. Open the filter () beside **Select trial**. Under **By trial annotation**, add `exclude` to **Excluding tags**.
1. [Check and export the selection](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/data-filtering/#every-task-ends-the-same-way).

For a trial with several screens, tag the whole trial. A tag on one screen does not exclude the trial.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/favorites_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/favorites.mp4)

*The recording shows favorites and tags. For the selection above, use the `exclude` tag and **Excluding tags**.*

# Find trials with specific fixation patterns

Locate trials containing particular fixation patterns.

Before you start, switch to **Full** at the top of the **Scanpath View** ([Essentials and Full](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/#essentials-and-full)).

1. Open **Filters & highlights** ▾ → **Fixations**.

1. Set the **Mode** of the category you need to **Highlight**:

   - **Short** or **Long**, with a duration threshold in **ms**
   - **Outside the text**, for fixations in no word box
   - **Near a blink**, if your data has a blink column

1. Step through the trials. In **Annotations**, tag those that meet your analysis criteria, for example `include`.

1. Open the filter () beside **Select trial**. Under **By trial annotation**, add `include` to **With any of these tags**.

1. [Check and export the selection](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/data-filtering/#every-task-ends-the-same-way).

# Select participants by a field

Select participants using metadata such as native language, age or group.

Before you start, switch to **Full** at the top of the **Scanpath View** ([Essentials and Full](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/#essentials-and-full)).

1. Attach a participant metadata table, with one row per participant and a participant ID column. When you add a dataset, use **Metadata** → **Participants**. For a loaded dataset, use **Data Management** → **Edit dataset** → **Data tables & column mapping**.
1. Open the filter () beside **Select trial** and find **By participant**.
1. Choose a field and the values or range to keep.
1. Check the remaining participant IDs and [export the selection](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/data-filtering/#every-task-ends-the-same-way).

To also apply trial-level quality criteria, follow [Exclude unsuitable trials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/data-filtering/exclude-unsuitable-trials/index.md).

  GIF, MP4 or interactive HTML.

# Export a replay

Save an animated reading for a talk or supplement.

Before you start, switch to **Full** at the top of the **Scanpath View** ([Essentials and Full](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/#essentials-and-full)).

1. Pick a trial in the **Scanpath View** and choose **Animation**.
1. In **Animation settings** → **Replay**, set the **Speed**. Turn on the layers you want to show.
1. Open the **Export** tab. Under **Current figure**, set **Download format** to **GIF**, **MP4** or **HTML**.
1. Download the replay. GIF and MP4 play at the selected speed. HTML keeps the interactive playback controls.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/replay-export_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/replay-export.mp4)

*Exporting a GIF. The rendering wait is shortened in this recording.*

For [GIF/MP4 export from Python](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/exporting/#replays-as-gif-or-mp4), see Export and share.

# Export every trial

Build a ZIP of static figures and data tables for a set of trials.

Before you start, switch to **Full** at the top of the **Scanpath View** ([Essentials and Full](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/#essentials-and-full)).

1. [Set the figure's design](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/exporting-figures/export-one-figure/#1-choose-the-view) once. Each exported trial uses that design, without animation or a comparison partner.
1. Open the **Export** tab. Under **Export bundle** → **Trials to include**, choose **This trial**, **All filtered trials**, **All trials of one participant**, **All trials of one text** or **All trials, ignoring filters**.
1. Choose the **Figure formats** and, under **Also include**, the tables and their **Table format**. Check the **File path pattern**. To edit individual layers later, turn on **Layers as separate files**.
1. Click **Build export**, download the bundle, and inspect one exported figure.

For PNGs, turn on **Smaller PNG files** to reduce file size at the same resolution. This adds encoding time. Images over 16.8 megapixels use the standard encoding to limit memory use. Outside the app, `scanpath-studio render --compact-png` and `save_figure(..., compact_png=True)` do the same for one figure and its layers. **PNG scale** controls resolution separately. A scale of 1 writes one pixel per figure pixel, and the default scale of 2 doubles both dimensions.

Large bundles are kept on temporary disk and download as one ZIP in a new tab. Keep the Export panel open until the download finishes. If your browser cannot stream the ZIP, the download page offers numbered parts and instructions for joining them.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/export-bundle_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/export-bundle.mp4)

*Exporting figures and tables for the bundled demo's trials. The build is sped up in this recording.*

Keep each trial's `plot_config.json` for the design, `README.md` for the build details and `index.csv` for the file list and failures. Keep your original data and record its version and the selected trial filters separately.

For a [scripted batch](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/exporting/#batch-pattern), use the Python recipe in Export and share.

# Export one figure

Save a scanpath, heatmap or comparison at the size you need.

In either mode, use the view tiles to choose a figure. For **Compare readings** and **My views**, switch to **Full** at the top of the **Scanpath View** ([Essentials and Full](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/#essentials-and-full)).

## 1. Choose the view

Pick a trial in the **Scanpath View**. Choose a **View** tile, or set the layers in Full. Turn on **Compare** if the figure needs two readings. Check that text and markers are readable and nothing is clipped.

## 2. Set the format and size

Open the **Export** tab and find **Current figure**. Choose the **Download format**:

| Output             | Format     |
| ------------------ | ---------- |
| Image              | PNG        |
| Vector figure      | SVG or PDF |
| Interactive figure | HTML       |

For a print PNG, set **Width** and **DPI**. For HTML that opens offline, tick **Self-contained HTML**.

## 3. Download

Click the download button for the chosen format, such as **⬇ Download PNG**.

\[!\[

\](../../../assets/workflows/export-figure_poster.webp)\](../../../assets/workflows/export-figure.mp4)

*Exporting a PNG at 180 mm and 300 dpi.*

## 4. Reuse the design or share the figure

- **My views** in the Plot controls saves the look for other trials.
- **Share** → **Link** reopens the trial and its settings. For data you imported, send the source files and tell the recipient the dataset name shown in the link. They can open the link after importing the files under that name. If a comparison uses two imported datasets, send both. Someone who has only A can open its trial and return to the link after adding B. Your own copy of the link still works if you rename either dataset later.
- [**Share** → **Code**](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/exporting/#from-the-app-to-a-script) gives Python or CLI code that redraws the figure.
- **Share** → **Settings file** → **Download settings** saves the settings, and **Restore settings** loads them again.

# Feature guides

Each guide explains one part of the app, with Python and CLI examples where they apply. For step-by-step workflows, see the [tutorials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/index.md).

- **[Scanpath visualization](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/index.md)**

  Explore layers and filters, replay a reading, or compare readings from one or two datasets.

- **[Data Management](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/loading-data/index.md)**

  Open a public dataset or import your files, check the column mapping, and enter the recording setup.

- **[Corpus Analysis](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/corpus-workspace/index.md)**

  Explore the reading measures in your data by text, participant or group.

- **[Export and share](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/exporting/index.md)**

  Figure downloads, share links and code, batch export and replay export.

# Corpus Analysis

Open **Corpus Analysis** to compare a reading measure across the trials in your current selection. The pool beside the dataset picker shows how many trials and participants your filters include.

## Compare the corpus

Choose **Texts** to compare passages or **Participants** to compare readers. The chart opens with a reading measure from your Words table. Use **Reading measure** to change it.

| Destination      | Dot                                        | Line                               |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
| **Texts**        | Mean across participants who read the text | Lowest to highest participant mean |
| **Participants** | Mean across that participant’s readings    | Lowest to highest reading mean     |

Each reading contributes the mean of its finite word values across all its screens. When a participant reads a text more than once, their reading means are averaged before they contribute to the text mean.

The chart starts with the 12 highest means. Select a dot to see the exact mean, range and number of observations. Use **Find a text** or **Find a participant** to inspect any ID, including one outside the first 12. **Table and downloads** includes every group with the required IDs, even those with no recorded values. Rates appear as percentages on screen and as proportions from 0 to 1 in the CSV.

Text summaries use the Text ID mapped in the Words table. Without one, **Participants** opens first and **Texts** lets you inspect a single reading. The summary excludes shared stimulus values copied across readers. Older saved datasets that predate this mapping information use their stored text IDs.

## Choose a view

Beside **Texts**, choose **Open word profile** to see where in a passage the measure changes. Beside **Participants**, **Open participant profile** compares one reader’s word values with the rest of the selected participants. If you selected a dot or used the search box, the profile opens for that text or participant. It uses the measure shown in the summary. Use **Back to texts** or **Back to participants** to return to the comparison.

In a participant profile, the wider parts of a violin show where more duration observations fall. A skip or regression rate has a percentage and the word counts behind it. Each measured word counts equally here, so longer readings can carry more weight than in the participant summary.

Open **Chart settings** to change the **View**. In a word profile, **Aggregate** sets how values are combined, **Spread** controls the shaded band, and **Min participants per word** sets how many readers must contribute.

**Readings behind a word** shows the source measurements and the value each participant contributes after combining repeated readings. A blank or infinite measurement contributes no value. The profile leaves a gap at a word below the participant threshold. When two readings of a text differ in their wording or layout, **Measure on the stimulus** lets you choose which version to tint.

## Include reading measures in your Words table

Word-level views use the [reading measures in your data](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/loading-data/#reading-measures), such as first fixation duration or total fixation duration. Map those columns when you import. Views of single fixations, such as **Fixation duration over time**, use the Fixations table.

## Compare groups

Choose **Groups** to see the two group means and their difference. Open **Edit groups** to change which readings belong to A and B. **Split a field** uses the values of a column. **Independent filter sets** lets you choose participants, texts or conditions separately for each group. To examine the first group on its own, turn off **Compare two groups**. For skip and regression rates, **Group means & difference** shows each mean as a percentage and their difference in percentage points. A word-by-word comparison across readings needs a shared Text ID in the Words table.

For a repeated-measures design, **Within-participant contrast** shows each participant's mean in A and B and the difference A − B. The summary averages only complete pairs. The CSV keeps readers who are missing either condition.

In **Edit filters**, **Study inclusion and exclusions** downloads participant and reading counts for the active pool. The separate per-reading file names all matching exclusion reasons, so a reading that fails two rules counts only once.

## Save results

In **Texts** or **Participants**, open **Table and downloads** below the comparison. Detailed analyses that produce a table have a **Download results** menu. The CSV saves the values. **Download recipe (JSON)** records the dataset, trial filters, analysis choices and counts. Keep the source files with the recipe to rerun the analysis.

A cohort profile's **Methods draft** records its measure, grouping, normalization, spread, reader threshold, trial filters and software version. **Compare profile revisions** saves a separate snapshot with individual reader IDs and measurements. After correcting a source file, open an earlier snapshot there to see which readings or word values changed.

### Rerun an overview or word profile

Save the recipe alongside the CSV from a text or participant summary, a **Cohort profile**, or **Groups → Difference word profile**. For a difference profile, the recipe records each group’s constraints and which group was subtracted. New recipes save the column mappings, filename-derived columns and character-box merges used at import. Supply the original files to reproduce the CSV.

```
scanpath-studio recipe profile.recipe.json --words words.csv --fixations fixations.csv -o profile.csv
```

For the bundled demo, use `--sample` in place of the table paths. If you filtered by participant, trial or text metadata, supply the original table with `--participant-metadata`, `--trial-metadata` or `--text-metadata`. For a star or tag filter, supply the dataset’s exported annotations with `--annotations`. New recipes also record a checksum of the CSV. If the rows or values differ, the command reports the mismatch before writing the output. Older recipes have no checksum. Supply their original mappings if needed, and download a fresh recipe when one of their filter labels is ambiguous. In Python, pass the decoded recipe or its path and the normalized frames to run_analysis_recipe.

## Plot a summary in code

Start from a tidy summary table, such as a **Cohort profile** table downloaded from Corpus Analysis. A word profile needs `word_id` and `value` columns, with optional `lo` and `hi` for a band. The downloaded table names the word ID column as your data does, so rename it to `word_id` if needed. For a text or participant summary CSV of skip or regression rates, use `kind="overview"` with `as_percent=True` in Python, or `--kind overview --percent` with the CLI. Set `series_col` or `--series-col` to the CSV’s text or participant ID column. For a trend over trial order, see [Across the experiment](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/gallery/across-experiment/index.md).

Python and CLI: word profile

```
import pandas as pd
import scanpath_studio as sps

profile = pd.read_csv("profile.csv")
fig = sps.plot_corpus_figure(
    profile, kind="profile", measure_label="Total fixation duration (ms)"
)
sps.save_figure(fig, "profile.html")
```

```
scanpath-studio corpus --input profile.csv --kind profile \
  --measure-label "Total fixation duration (ms)" -o profile.html
```

[API parameters](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/api/#scanpath_studio.api.plot_corpus_figure) · [CLI options](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/cli/#corpus)

# Export and share

Save a figure, export many trials at once, or reuse a view in the app or in code.

## In the app

| Goal                                  | Where                                            |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Save the figure or replay on screen   | **Export** → **Current figure**                  |
| Prepare a figure for a paper or slide | **Export** → **Prepare figure for export**       |
| Export many trials and their tables   | **Export** → **Export bundle**                   |
| Share a view or copy its code         | **Share** → **Link** or **Code**                 |
| Reuse the figure settings             | **My presets**, or **Share** → **Settings file** |

To export multiple trials, switch to Full and open **Export bundle**. Essentials offers **Current figure** for the figure or replay on screen.

For step-by-step instructions, see the [export tutorials](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/exporting-figures/index.md).

## Prepare a paper figure or slide

Open **Scanpath → Export → Prepare figure for export**. The preview shows the current reading, comparison or replay still. For a corpus chart, open **Prepare figure for export** directly beneath the chart. Choose **Download PNG** for a slide or document, or switch the file format to SVG, PDF or TIFF.

- **Crop** lets you draw a rectangle, select a word span when words are available, or use the scanpath’s current zoom. Under **Label events**, pin a fixation or saccade and drag its label into position.
- **Caption and description** suggests a caption and alternative text. Edit them, download both as text, or include the caption below the artwork.
- For a replay, **Replay clip** lets you choose the interval, speed and poster frame. **Prepare MP4 and poster** produces a ZIP with the clip, poster and editable file. Rendering PDF or video in the app requires Chromium on the server.
- When a journal specifies dimensions, open **Print settings** to set the width, resolution or minimum text size. In Full mode on the Scanpath View, **Use this size for batch export** prints each bundle figure at the prepared artwork’s width and resolution; the crop, labels and caption stay with the prepared figure.

Under **Save or open**, save a copy on this device or download an editable file for a coauthor. The file includes the plotted data, tooltip fields and embedded images. Open it here, under **Data Management → Saved work → Saved figures**, or via **Share → Settings file**. A Share link opens the editor on the source view. An editable file also restores your crop, labels and caption. Older files containing several figures open with their saved layout.

## Reproduce a coauthor's results

The installed package includes a fictional three-reader study, its raw tables, recording setup, one tagged exclusion, figure settings and a cohort recipe. To work through it in an empty folder, copy the example and follow its README.

```
python -c "from importlib.resources import files; from shutil import copytree; copytree(files('scanpath_studio') / 'sample_data' / 'coauthor', 'canal-study')"
```

The commands recreate a figure and a two-word results table. A checksum from the original release lets the recipient verify the table byte for byte.

## Cite what you export

Files saved through **Export** include citation information in their metadata. To add a visible credit to the figure, use **Figure** → **Title & labels** → **Credit**.

- **Cite**, under each download and in **Share** → **Code**, gives a one-line figure credit, the APA reference and BibTeX, and `.bib` and `.ris` files for Zotero, Mendeley or EndNote. For the bundled demo, OneStop or PoTeC, it cites the corpus too.
- Each export bundle includes `CITATION.bib` and citation instructions in `README.md`.
- **Figure** → **Title & labels** → **Credit** adds a small *Made with Scanpath Studio* line under the plot, for a figure shared without its caption. In code, pass `show_credit=True`, or `--credit` to `render`.
- In code, cite and `scanpath-studio cite` print the citation.

\[!\[

\](../../assets/workflows/share-link_poster.webp)\](../../assets/workflows/share-link.mp4)

A link can find an imported dataset on the same computer after you rename it. On another computer, import the sender’s data under the name in the link. The link checks that the recording tables match, including those for a second imported dataset in a comparison. Older links can open without checking the tables. [All controls → Under the plot](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/#under-the-plot) says what the recipient needs.

## Reproduce a figure

Open **Share** → **Code** and copy the Python or CLI code. It includes the figure's settings and your column mapping. The compact code includes changes that affect this view. For example, a comparison uses each scanpath's own fixation color for its index numbers. Select **Show every option** to include the other accepted figure settings. For a dataset you imported, replace the placeholder file paths with your own. [Render in code](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/#render-in-code) shows a minimal example.

For a PNG at print size, pass `width_mm` and `dpi` to `save_figure`, or `--width-mm` and `--dpi` to `render`. To edit the layers in a vector editor, save each layer to a separate file with `save_figure_layers` or `render --separable-layers`. In the app's export bundle, this is **Layers as separate files**.

## Batch export

In the app, **Export bundle** → **Trials to include** picks the trials: **This trial**, **All filtered trials**, **All trials of one participant**, **All trials of one text** or **All trials, ignoring filters**. Open **Preview bundle contents** to see the selected readings, their filenames and the columns in their tables. A word-measures CSV can contain the original stimulus words even when the figure masks them. When you select specific screens, the bundle includes notes on those screens and their parent trials.

When you export all screens, rows with no Screen ID are included once in the trial’s tables. Selecting specific screens includes only rows assigned to those screens. A screen with raw gaze alone has its own sample table.

If a figure fails, the download includes the files that succeeded. With the same data and settings still open, choose **Retry failed figure files**. The app retries each missing format or layer and keeps the successful files. If it could not split a figure into layers, it tries that step again. Check `index.csv` for any files that still failed. Stopping a retry leaves the previous download available.

CSV bundles include `columns.json` and an editable `read_csv.R`. In R, set the working directory to the extracted bundle and run `source("read_csv.R")` with the jsonlite package installed. The example preserves reader IDs such as `01` and `1` as text. A blank measurement becomes `NA` and zero stays zero.

For a scripted batch, loop over the trial list.

Python: one HTML figure per trial

```
from pathlib import Path

import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
out = Path("figures")
out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

for pid, tid in sps.list_trials(words, fixations).itertuples(index=False):
    # Each demo reading has several screens; this saves its paragraph.
    fig = sps.plot_scanpath(words, fixations, pid, tid, screen="Paragraph")
    sps.save_figure(fig, out / f"{pid}_{tid}.html")
```

Use the [data loaders](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/loading-data/#load-and-inspect-in-code) for your own files. The CLI's `render` writes one trial per run.

## Replay export

With **Animation** selected, **Export** → **Current figure** saves the replay as HTML, GIF or MP4. In a saved HTML replay, **Previous fixation** and **Next fixation** move to individual onsets and show the fixation’s duration and assigned word when available. The time slider scrubs through the whole reading. Each frame of a GIF or MP4 shows the state reached at that frame’s start, and the last frame shows the complete scanpath. With a low frame cap, a fixation that begins between two frames first shows in the later one.

The CLI’s `render --animate` saves interactive HTML. For a GIF or MP4 in Python:

Python: save a GIF or MP4

```
from pathlib import Path

import scanpath_studio as sps
from scanpath_studio.animation_export import export_animation

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
replay = sps.animate_scanpath(
    words, fixations, "l37_273", "l37_273_2_1_1_Ele", screen="Paragraph"
)
Path("replay.mp4").write_bytes(export_animation(replay, fmt="mp4"))
```

Use `fmt="gif"` and a `.gif` filename for GIF output.

[Export setup and troubleshooting](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/faq/#export-fails) · [Python save options](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/api/#save) · [CLI options](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/cli/#common-tasks)

## Proof two manuscript panels

In **Compare**, choose two readings with the same screen dimensions and a side-by-side or stacked layout. In **Export → Current figure → Manuscript panel proof**, enter the total print width. The proof shows the resulting label sizes in points and the numeric color limits shared by the two panels. Use the Fixations or Heatmap controls to choose your own limits.

**Prepare manuscript SVG** provides the lettered vector panels at that physical width. **Save panel settings** preserves their order, styles, width and selected limits. Open the settings file in **Share → File**, replace one reading and prepare the revised SVG.

# Data Management

Load your own data, open a public dataset, or try the bundled demo.

## Choose a dataset

Pick a dataset in **Select dataset** above the plot or open **Dataset library** on the **Data Management** page.

- **Bundled demo** includes 24 readings by two L1 English readers of 12 OneStop texts. Each reading keeps every screen the reader saw: the article's title (first paragraph only), the question preview, the paragraph, the question, the answers and the feedback. Each screen shows the experiment's own stimulus image, placed where the experiment drew it. The 1,000 Hz EyeLink samples cover each screen from its onset to the response that ended it. Each sample keeps its timestamp, screen coordinates, pupil area in tracker units and tracked eye. During tracking loss the coordinates and the pupil area are blank.
- **Hand-drawn sample**: a scanpath drawn by hand over a short English text, which you can edit.
- Public datasets: OneStop and PoTeC. In the desktop app or a pip install, each downloads the first time you open it.
- **+** → **Import files**: your own tables.
- **+** → **Draw a scanpath**: write a text and place its fixations by hand.

### Draw a scanpath

Choose **+ → Draw a scanpath**, then type your passage. In **Draw** mode, click the words in reading order. Click a word twice for two visits, or click the space between words for a fixation without a target. For a regular sequence, **Reset to one fixation per word** places a 220 ms fixation on each word.

Use **Select & move** to drag a marker. The **Fixation** list lets you select visits that land on top of one another. Change **Duration (ms)** and use **Play preview** to check the timing. The **Fixation table** also accepts keyboard edits. Leaving both coordinates empty places the fixation at the center of its target word.

**Save dataset** opens the figure. To revise it, go to **Data Management** and click **Edit drawing** beside its name. **Save changes** updates the drawing, and **Save as copy** keeps a separate version. For another computer, download the editable draft from **Share** and open it with **Load a saved draft** in the drawing editor.

### OneStop

The bundled demo comes from [OneStop Eye Movements](https://github.com/lacclab/OneStop-Eye-Movements) (Berzak et al., 2025), an English corpus with 360 participants. The full corpus is available as four public datasets: **OneStop · Ordinary reading**, **OneStop · Information seeking**, **OneStop · Repeated reading** and **OneStop · Information seeking (repeated)**. Each downloads once from [OSF](https://osf.io/2prdq/).

## What your data needs

Start with a Fixations, Words or Raw gaze table. You can add the other tables whenever you need them.

To try a right-to-left passage, import the bundled `sample_data/mixed_script_words.csv` and `sample_data/mixed_script_fixations.csv`. The two synthetic lines combine Hebrew, Arabic, English, digits and punctuation. Use an 800 × 250 px canvas to see the recorded layout. The tenth fixation revisits the Arabic word on the second line.

| Table                  | Contents                                                       |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Fixations              | One row per fixation: trial ID, duration, and x/y or a word ID |
| Words (interest areas) | One row per word: trial ID, word ID and word box               |
| Raw gaze               | One row per gaze sample: trial ID, x and y                     |
| Participants           | One row per participant, with metadata                         |
| Trials                 | One row per trial, with metadata                               |
| Texts                  | One row per text, with metadata                                |

The app recognizes column names from common eye-tracker exports. Check the mapping when you import. To keep condition labels and other columns, pick them under **Extra fields to keep**. You can filter, sort and group trials by any metadata field.

### Files and units

- CSV, TSV, TXT, Parquet, Feather, Excel, or a ZIP of these files
- Positions in pixels
- Times in milliseconds. A time column whose header names its unit, such as `[s]`, `[μs]` or `[ns]`, is converted.
- Word boxes as `x/y/width/height` or EyeLink's `IA_LEFT/RIGHT/TOP/BOTTOM`
- Word IDs as numbers, or as text such as `w1`. Text IDs must match exactly in the Fixations and Words tables. With text IDs, the order of the rows in the Words table sets the word order.
- Several files for one table, such as one file per trial, are stacked into one table, with each file's name in a `source_file` column. When an ID is only in the file name, use **Derive columns from text** to extract it into a column you can map. When you click **Apply**, a derived column named like an ID, such as `participant`, `trial` or `stimulus`, fills that ID field if it is empty.
- Trial and Text IDs are matched exactly, so spell them the same way in both tables, including upper and lower case. The import screen says when they differ only in case.
- Words tables with one box per character, as in Chinese or Japanese: turn on **Merge character boxes into word boxes**. The import screen suggests it when a word's rows are at different positions.

### Trials over several screens

Map the **Screen ID** field in your tables. A column named `screen_index` sets the order of the screens. Without one, the screens are ordered by where they first appear, using the Fixations table if available. The app draws one screen at a time.

### Reading measures

Corpus Analysis uses the per-word reading measures in your Words table, such as first fixation duration or total fixation duration. Map them when you import. EyeLink's `IA_*` columns are detected.

## Add your own data

For a walkthrough inside the import wizard, choose **Setup help → Show setup guide**.

1. Choose **+** → **Import files** and name the dataset.
1. Upload your tables and check the column mapping.
1. Under **Recording setup**, enter the **Screen**, **Monitor width** and **Text size** if you know them.
1. Optionally, in the desktop app or a local install, attach the stimulus images from a folder.
1. Click **Add dataset**, then **Open in Scanpath View** to see its first trial. You can also open the figure from **Data Management → Current dataset**.

To import similar files again, click **Download setup file** before **Add dataset**. Next time, choose **Start from** → **A setup file** and upload your tables: the column mapping, derived columns, character-box merge and recording setup are filled in.

\[!\[

\](../../assets/workflows/add-your-data_poster.webp)\](../../assets/workflows/add-your-data.mp4)

## Load and inspect in code

Load the same files in a script. The loaders detect column names the same way the app does.

Python and CLI

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_scanpath_data("ia.csv", "fixations.csv")
print(sps.list_trials(words, fixations))
```

```
scanpath-studio render --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv --list-trials
scanpath-studio check --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv
```

For raw gaze, metadata and explicit column mappings, see the [loaders](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/api/#load-your-data) and [CLI input options](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/cli/#flags-input).

### Add a dataset from a script

On your own computer, a script can add a dataset to the app's list. Use it to prepare the tables in code and then look at them in the app. Start the app afterwards and it opens on the new dataset. If the app is already open, reload its browser tab right away: changes you make in it before the reload are not saved.

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

sps.add_dataset(
    "Pilot 3",
    words="ia.csv",
    fixations="fixations.csv",
    canvas_size=(1920, 1080),
)
```

```
scanpath-studio add "Pilot 3" --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv --canvas 1920x1080
```

The tables load as `load_scanpath_data` loads them, and the dataset is saved with your other [saved work](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/cli/#cache). Adding again under the same name is an error unless you pass `replace=True` (`--replace`). That swaps the tables and keeps the dataset's annotations, metadata tables, share links, description and recording setup, unless you give a new description or screen. Without a screen size, the app uses one the data records, or estimates one from the extent of the data. To set it later, use **Edit dataset**. See add_dataset for every option.

To open the app on one reading of it, with the figure you want, write a link. It names the dataset, the participant and trial, and the figure in `plot_scanpath`'s options or `render`'s flags. From the CLI, `open` opens it in your browser, and starts the app first if it isn't running.

```
url = sps.app_link("Pilot 3", "p07", "t12", show_heatmap=True)
```

```
scanpath-studio open "Pilot 3" -p p07 -t t12 --heatmap
```

The link is the one **Share** → **Link** writes for that view, so settings it leaves out keep the values the app has. See app_link and [`open`](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/cli/#open).

To take a dataset off the list again, use remove_dataset or `scanpath-studio remove "Pilot 3"`. Any dataset you added can be removed this way, with its annotations and metadata tables, as its **Remove** on the Data Management page does.

### Annotations from a script

A script can also read and write the favorites, tags and notes on a dataset you added. A quality-control script can tag the readings it flags, and reviewers find them in the app with the tag filter. An analysis can read back what the reviewers marked.

```
import pandas as pd
import scanpath_studio as sps

flags = pd.DataFrame(
    {"participant_id": ["p01", "p02"], "trial_id": ["3", "7"], "tags": "Short"}
)
result = sps.write_annotations("Pilot 3", flags)
print(result.unknown)  # readings the dataset does not have, left out

marked = sps.read_annotations("Pilot 3")
excluded = marked[marked["tags"].map(lambda tags: "To exclude" in tags)]
```

```
scanpath-studio annotations import "Pilot 3" flags.csv
scanpath-studio annotations export "Pilot 3" -o annotations.csv
```

The table has one row per reading: `participant_id`, `trial_id`, `screen_id` for one screen of a trial recorded over several, and any of `favorite`, `tags` and `note`. In a CSV file, separate tags with `;`. The app's exported `annotations.json` works too. Writing adds a reading's tags to the ones it has, and a favorite or note you give replaces its own. Pass `mode="replace"` (`--replace`) to make the dataset's annotations exactly the ones given; it is refused when none of the given readings is in the dataset. A reading the dataset does not have is left out and listed. An app already open shows the new annotations once its browser tab is reloaded. See write_annotations for every option.

## Manage datasets

**Current dataset** opens on **Overview**. It shows how many participants, trials and texts are in your selection and the average number of trials per participant. Fixation and word averages count trials that contain those rows. **Eye-tracking data** shows the row and trial counts for each table. Scanpath trial filters apply to these counts.

Click a table name to jump to its rows. **Tables** shows fixations, words, raw gaze samples, participants, trials and texts on one page. When you attach a participant, trial or text metadata file, that table shows the complete file.

**Data checks** looks for unusable values in the whole dataset, including trials outside the filters. **Annotations** lets you review, import and export the dataset’s favorites, tags and notes. A script can read and write them too; see [Annotations from a script](#annotations-from-a-script).

To switch datasets, open **Dataset library**. Search by name or filter by source, then click a dataset to open its overview. **Saved work** shows what will reopen next time. On a local install, **Dataset downloads** lists the public datasets on disk and lets you choose where future downloads go.

Use **Edit dataset** to change its name, column mapping, recording setup or metadata, then click **Save changes**. **Download setup file** saves the mapping, recording setup and character-box merge, so you can apply them to similar data.

The editor offers only the columns kept when the dataset was added. To use a column that isn't listed, remove the dataset and add it again from its files, mapping the column or keeping it under **Extra fields to keep**.

Under **Data checks**, **Compare with planned trials (optional)** accepts a CSV with `participant_id` and `trial_id`. Add `screen_id` to check an individual screen. Enter a reason in `planned_omission` for readings you intended to omit and leave it blank for the rest. The report distinguishes missing readings, unscheduled recordings, and readings with raw gaze alone. **Review affected readings** shows all the rows behind a finding, one reading at a time, while your trial filters stay in place.

Excel imports use the first worksheet and show its name. ID columns preserve literal labels such as `01` and `NA`. Leave a cell empty for a missing ID. On restoring a pilot setup, the wizard names files whose headers or time units differ from the saved mapping.

Under **Name → Dataset citation**, an upload can carry its title, authors or lab, version, DOI, and preferred credit. An unpublished study can supply just its preferred wording. Reopen **Edit dataset** to revise the credit. **Cite** and the export bundle include these references alongside the software citation.

# Scanpath visualization

1. Views and Help.
1. The **Essentials | Full** switch ([below](#essentials-and-full)).
1. The trial control bar: dataset, trial, screen, sort (⇅) and filter ().
1. The trial's summary.
1. The figure.
1. Plot controls.
1. The tabs: Annotations, Stimulus & context, Comparisons, Export and Share.

The **Scanpath View** draws one reading at a time, at the size of the screen it was recorded on.

Looking for a specific button?

[All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md) lists every button and setting on this view, menu by menu, with a picture of each menu. Search it for what you want to change, such as *saccade color* or *legend position*.

## Essentials and Full

The Scanpath View opens in **Essentials**, with the main controls for exploring a reading. Switch to **Full** in the top bar whenever you want more options. The app remembers your choice in this browser.

Essentials shows:

- the dataset and trial pickers with **◀ ▶**;
- the plot, which starts with a replay on a new visit;
- the **Animation** tile, five static views and the **Palette** tiles;
- the **Export** tab, for the figure on screen, and **Share**.

The **More** buttons show which additional controls are available in Full and offer **Switch to Full**. Both modes keep the selected view and palette. An active comparison keeps its switch in Essentials. Settings you chose in Full, such as trial filters, remain active in Essentials; a short note tells you when they apply. Starting a tutorial from **Help** switches to Full for the current visit. **Corpus Analysis** and **Data Management** are the same in both modes.

To open a mode for one visit, add `?ui=full` or `?ui=essentials` to the app's address (use `&` if the address already has a `?`). This leaves your saved choice unchanged. Links created with **Share** use the recipient's own mode.

The numbered regions above and the rest of this guide describe Full.

## Choose a trial

Pick a trial in **Select trial** above the plot, or step through the list with **◀ ▶**. The filter () beside it narrows the list by text, participant, condition or annotation, and **⇅** sorts it. On a trial recorded over several screens, **Screen** picks the screen to draw. When several participants have the same trial ID, the list shows each reading with its participant in brackets, such as `3 [p2]`.

[All controls → Trial control bar](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/#trial-control-bar) describes each control.

### Keyboard shortcuts

| With focus on                                    | Keys                             | Action                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| The page, plot background or trial arrow buttons | `Left` / `Right`                 | Previous or next trial in the current list (A in Compare) |
| The page, plot background or trial arrow buttons | `Shift`+`Left` / `Shift`+`Right` | Previous or next trial for B in Compare                   |
| The page or plot background                      | `Space`                          | Play or pause the replay                                  |
| The **Replay time** slider                       | `Left` / `Right`                 | Pause and step one frame                                  |
| The **Replay time** slider                       | `Home` / `End`                   | Jump to the first or last frame                           |
| The **Replay time** slider                       | `Space`                          | Play or pause from the current frame                      |

With **A and B together** on, either pair of trial shortcuts steps both readings. Use `Tab` and `Shift`+`Tab` to reach the replay controls. The slider keys also work in downloaded HTML replays.

## Control the layers

Both modes start with the same **Presets** tiles and **Palette**. In Full, use **Find a setting** to jump to a control by name, or open **Layers** to change what appears in the plot. Click a layer’s name to edit its settings or its switch to show or hide it. Choose **Axes** to chart the reading by fixation order or time. **Figure** holds the settings for the whole plot, including framing, titles and legends.

**Gaze over time** plots elapsed seconds along the horizontal axis and horizontal screen position in pixels on the vertical axis. The length of each horizontal bar shows how long the fixation lasted. Turn **Animation** on to replay the reading on the text, then off to return to the same chart. **Custom** brings back your last hand-edited figure.

| Section                  | What it controls                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Presets**              | switch **Animation** on or off, or choose **Scanpath**, **Heatmap**, **Illustration**, **Gaze over time** or **Custom** |
| **My presets**           | save a named preset, apply it to another reading, or share it                                                           |
| **Palette**              | choose **Colorblind-safe**, **Grayscale**, or **High contrast**                                                         |
| **Compare readings**     | add a second reading over this one, beside it, or below it                                                              |
| **Playback settings**    | set playback speed, autoplay, and frame quality                                                                         |
| **Fixations**            | the fixation markers: color, shape and size, and the fixation index                                                     |
| **Saccades**             | the saccade lines and arrows, in one color, by direction or by saccade type                                             |
| **Stimulus**             | the text (or redacted blocks), highlighted words, the stimulus image, the font and the background                       |
| **Word boxes**           | each word's box: outline and fill, color and opacity                                                                    |
| **Heatmap**              | where fixations concentrate, by fixation count or duration                                                              |
| **Raw gaze**             | the gaze samples as recorded                                                                                            |
| **Filters & highlights** | which fixations and saccades are drawn, and which stand out                                                             |
| **Axes**                 | chart presets, X and Y fields, and the coordinate grid                                                                  |
| **Figure**               | screen framing, title and labels, hover fields and legends                                                              |

[All controls → Plot controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/#plot-controls) describes every setting in each menu.

\[!\[

\](../../assets/workflows/plot-controls_poster.webp)\](../../assets/workflows/plot-controls.mp4)

## Under the plot

| Tab                    | What it is for                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Annotations**        | Star, tag and write notes on the trial, to find or filter it later.                                                                                                                                              |
| **Stimulus & context** | The trial's context, such as its title, question and answers, and its highlighted word spans.                                                                                                                    |
| **Comparisons**        | Show the other trials that share a field with this one, such as other readings of the same text, in a grid of small figures.                                                                                     |
| **Export**             | Download the figure on screen (PNG, SVG, PDF or HTML) or its replay (HTML, GIF or MP4), or build a zip bundle of figures and data for many trials.                                                               |
| **Share**              | **Link** reopens this trial with these settings for anyone who has the same dataset. **Code** gives the Python or CLI code that redraws the figure. **Settings file** saves the plot settings and restores them. |

[All controls → Under the plot](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/#under-the-plot) lists each tab's controls.

Watch the tabs under the figure

\[!\[

\](../../assets/workflows/subtabs_poster.webp)\](../../assets/workflows/subtabs.mp4)

## Render in code

Set up a figure in the app, then open **Share** → **Code** for the Python or CLI code that redraws it. For a dataset you imported, replace the placeholder file paths with your own.

Python and CLI: render the demo

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(
    words, fixations, "l37_273", "l37_273_2_1_1_Ele", screen="Paragraph"
)
sps.save_figure(fig, "scanpath.html")
```

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_273 -t l37_273_2_1_1_Ele --screen Paragraph -o scanpath.html
```

For your own files, use the [data loaders](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/loading-data/#load-and-inspect-in-code). The [figure options table](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/api/#figure-options) lists every figure setting with its Python keyword and CLI flag. For more CLI examples, see [Common tasks](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/cli/#common-tasks).

The [gallery](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/gallery/index.md) shows how to make heatmaps, comparisons, replays and other figures in the app, the CLI and Python. For batch export and GIF or MP4 replays, see [Export and share](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/exporting/index.md).

## Back up your work

You can save each of these to a file and load it again:

| What                               | Where                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| figure settings                    | **Share** → **Settings file**                                            |
| favorites, tags and notes          | **Data Management** → **Current dataset** → **Annotations** → **Export** |
| column mapping and recording setup | **Edit dataset** → **Download setup file**                               |
| saved figure designs               | **My presets** → **Export**                                              |

Keep your source data alongside these files, and load the same dataset before restoring them. In the desktop app or a local install, the app also keeps your datasets, annotations and designs between sessions. See **Data Management** → **Saved work → Your session**.

# All controls

Find every control in the **Scanpath View**, in the order it appears on screen. Search this page (`Ctrl`+`F`, or `Cmd`+`F` on a Mac) for what you want to change, such as *colors*, *legends* or *axes*.

The view has two sets of controls:

- The **trial control bar**, above the plot, decides *what* you see: the dataset, the trial, and which trials are in the list.
- The **plot controls**, the column on the right, decide *how* it is drawn: each layer of the figure, its colors and sizes, and the figure as a whole.

Use the tabs under the plot to annotate the current trial, read its context, compare readings, export a figure or share the view. For how the parts fit together, see the [Scanpath visualization](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/index.md) guide.

For the corresponding Python keywords and CLI flags, use the [figure options table](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/api/#figure-options).

## Trial control bar

The bar above the plot: pick a dataset and a trial, step through the trials, and narrow, sort or label the list. Essentials has all of it except the slider, **⇅**, the filter () and the trial summary table with its pencil (), which are in Full.

| Control                                           | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Select dataset**                                | The dataset the view shows.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| → **Draw a scanpath**                             | Write a text and place its fixations by hand, as a new dataset.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| → **Import files**                                | Upload your own Fixations and Words tables as a new dataset.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Select trial**                                  | The trial to show. Click it and type to narrow the list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Slider                                            | Move through the trials in the list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **◀ ▶**                                           | The previous or next trial. You can also use `Left` and `Right` from the page or plot background.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **⇅** → **Sort trials by**                        | Reorder the trial list by a statistic (such as reading time), a participant, text or condition field, or a column of a metadata table you attached.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **⇅** → **Descending**                            | Reverse that order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| → **Text** / **Participant**                      | Keep only these texts or participants. Empty keeps all.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| → *a field of your data*                          | Keep only trials with these values, or, for a number, in this range.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| → **By participant** / **By trial** / **By text** | The same, for the columns of an attached metadata table.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| → **Favorites only**                              | Keep only starred trials.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| → **With any of these tags**                      | Keep only trials with any of these tags.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| → **Excluding tags**                              | Hide trials with any of these tags, such as *To exclude*.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| → **✕ Clear all filters**                         | Reset every filter in the panel.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| → **Show the trial summary above the plot**       | Show or hide the row of facts about the trial above the plot.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| → field lists                                     | Drag fields between *Shown* and *Available* to choose the trial summary's fields, and drag within *Shown* to reorder them. *Available* holds every field with one value per trial: participant, text and condition columns, the columns of any metadata table you attached, and statistics such as reading time and fixation count. |
| → **Field colors**                                | Give a field a highlight color. Its **✕** puts it back to the default gray.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| → **Refresh fields**                              | Check again which fields have one value per trial.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
