Requires `--label-a`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `--compare-legend` `--no-compare-legend` | switch                               | —           | Draw the Compare (A/B) legend, which names the two scanpaths. On by default; `--no-compare-legend` hides it. Also applies to `--animate`.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `--style-a`                              | `SPEC`                               | —           | Style for scanpath A, repeatable: KEY=VALUE[,...]. Colors (#RRGGBB): fix_color, saccade_color, box_color (word-box outline; default fix_color), box_fill_color (default `--word-box-fill-color`), raw_gaze_color (default fix_color). Also heatmap_colorscale (default `--heatmap-colorscale`, on the shared range), saccade_style (solid |
| `--style-b`                              | `SPEC`                               | —           | Style for scanpath B, repeatable: KEY=VALUE[,...]. Colors (#RRGGBB): fix_color, saccade_color, box_color (word-box outline; default fix_color), box_fill_color (default `--word-box-fill-color`), raw_gaze_color (default fix_color). Also heatmap_colorscale (default `--heatmap-colorscale`, on the shared range), saccade_style (solid |
| `--compare-fixation-flag`                | `SPEC`                               | —           | Filters & highlights for scanpath B only. Repeatable. Same SPEC as `--fixation-flag`, e.g. `--compare-fixation-flag` short=hide,threshold_ms=80. Replaces `--fixation-flag` for B.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--compare-saccade-classes`              | `CLASSES`                            | —           | The saccade types scanpath B draws, comma-separated, named as in `--saccade-classes`. Replaces `--saccade-classes` for B. Not with `--animate`, which draws every type.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `--compare-fix-index-range`              | `START:END`                          | —           | Draw only fixations START to END of scanpath B, counting from 1, both included. Replaces `--fix-index-range` for B.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--stimulus-image-b`                     | `PATH`                               | —           | Scanpath B's stimulus image, for a side-by-side or stacked comparison across two datasets, where each panel draws its image. Sized and placed like `--stimulus-image`.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `--stimulus-image-size-b`                | `WxH`                                | —           | Size of `--stimulus-image-b` in px (default: the PNG's pixel size, else `--compare-canvas`, else `--canvas`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `--stimulus-image-origin-b`              | `X,Y`                                | —           | Top-left corner of `--stimulus-image-b` in B's screen px (default: 0,0).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--compare-words`                        | `PATH [PATH ...]`                    | —           | The Words table for a second dataset, B's. Same formats and globbing as `--words`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--compare-fixations`                    | `PATH [PATH ...]`                    | —           | The Fixations table for a second dataset, B's. Same formats and globbing as `--fixations`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--compare-raw-gaze`                     | `PATH [PATH ...]`                    | —           | The Raw gaze table for the second dataset, drawn under B's scanpath. Same formats as `--raw-gaze`. | `--compare-word-schema`                  | `JSON`                               | —           | Column mapping for the `--compare-words` table, replacing auto-detection. Same form as `--word-schema`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `--compare-fix-schema`                   | `JSON`                               | —           | Column mapping for the `--compare-fixations` table, replacing auto-detection. | `--compare-raw-gaze-schema`              | `JSON`                               | —           | Column mapping for the `--compare-raw-gaze` table, replacing auto-detection. Same form as `--raw-gaze-schema`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `--compare-dataset-name`                 | `NAME`                               | `Dataset B` | Name of the second dataset, used in the trace names (default: 'Dataset B').                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `--compare-canvas`                       | `WxH`                                | —           | The second dataset's screen size in px, e.g. 1680x1050. Estimated from its data when left out. An overlay, or `--animate` with both scanpaths, checks it against `--canvas`.                                                                                                                                                              |

## corpus

`corpus` renders a styled corpus figure from a tidy CSV you already have, as plot_corpus_figure does. For `--kind profile` the CSV needs `word_id` and `value` columns.

```
scanpath-studio corpus --input profile.csv --kind profile --output profile.svg
```

To draw an overview CSV, pass its grouping column with `--series-col`. For example, this draws participant means and their observed ranges from a summary whose ID column is named `reader`.

```
scanpath-studio corpus --input overview.csv --kind overview --series-col reader \
  --measure-label "Total fixation duration (ms)" -o overview.html
```

| Option              | Value                                               | Default   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--input`           | `PATH`                                              | required  | The CSV. profile reads word_id and the value column, plus optional lo and hi; distribution reads the value column; difference reads word_id and diff. Overview reads the group column (`--series-col`), the mean (`--value-col`), lo and hi. |
| `--kind`            | `overview`, `profile`, `distribution`, `difference` | required  | A corpus overview, per-word profile, distribution or difference profile.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `-o` `--output`     | `PATH`                                              | required  | Output file; any extension save_figure writes (.html, .png, .svg, .pdf).                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `--measure-label`   | `MEASURE_LABEL`                                     | `Value`   | Axis and legend label for the value (default: Value).                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--series-col`      | `SERIES_COL`                                        | `series`  | Group ID for an overview, or column naming the overlaid series (default: series).                                                                                                                                                            |
| `--value-col`       | `VALUE_COL`                                         | `value`   | The value column (default: value).                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `--percent`         | switch                                              | —         | Show overview values and bounds stored as proportions (0–1) as percentages.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--primary-color`   | `PRIMARY_COLOR`                                     | —         | First series color (overview: #0072B2, other figures: #1f77b4).                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--secondary-color` | `SECONDARY_COLOR`                                   | `#e45756` | Second series color (default: #e45756).                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

## recipe

Recreate an **Overview**, **Cohort profile** or **Difference word profile** CSV from its downloaded JSON recipe and source tables. Recipes include the original column mappings. If raw gaze supplied the text IDs used by a metadata filter, pass its files with `--raw-gaze`. The command identifies any missing metadata or annotation input and verifies the regenerated CSV against the checksum in the recipe when available.

```
scanpath-studio recipe profile.recipe.json --words words.csv --fixations fixations.csv -o profile.csv
```

**Positional arguments**

| Option | Value         | Default  | Description                                      |
| ------ | ------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
|        | `RECIPE.json` | required | Analysis recipe downloaded from Corpus Analysis. |

**Options**

| Option                   | Value                       | Default  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--sample`               | switch                      | —        | Use the bundled demo.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `--words`                | `WORDS [WORDS ...]`         | —        | Original Words table(s).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `--fixations`            | `FIXATIONS [FIXATIONS ...]` | —        | Original Fixations table(s).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--raw-gaze`             | `RAW_GAZE [RAW_GAZE ...]`   | —        | Original raw gaze table(s) when a text metadata filter uses their IDs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--trial-parts-manifest` | `TRIAL_PARTS_MANIFEST`      | —        | Multipart trial manifest used at import.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `--word-schema`          | `JSON`                      | —        | Column mapping for the `--words` table, replacing auto-detection. A JSON object from each field to a column name, or the path of a JSON file holding one, e.g. '{"trial": "TRIAL_INDEX", "word_id": "IA_ID", ...}'. It is the dict api.load_scanpath_data takes. Needed only when a column isn't recognized, and the error then prints a mapping to start from.     |
| `--fix-schema`           | `JSON`                      | —        | Column mapping for the `--fixations` table, replacing auto-detection. A JSON object from each field to a column name, or the path of a JSON file holding one, e.g. '{"trial": "TRIAL_INDEX", "word_id": "IA_ID", ...}'. It is the dict api.load_scanpath_data takes. Needed only when a column isn't recognized, and the error then prints a mapping to start from. |
| `--keep-columns`         | `COLUMN [COLUMN ...]`       | —        | More columns to keep through loading, under the names they have in your files (e.g. a pupil size), from whichever table has them. Without it, loading keeps only the mapped and recognized fields. A kept fixation column can be used by `--color-by`, an axis or a hover. Same as keep_columns= in api.load_scanpath_data.                                         |
| `--participant-metadata` | `PARTICIPANT_METADATA`      | —        | The participant metadata table used by the recipe's filters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--trial-metadata`       | `TRIAL_METADATA`            | —        | The trial metadata table used by the recipe's filters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--text-metadata`        | `TEXT_METADATA`             | —        | The text metadata table used by the recipe's filters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `--annotations`          | `ANNOTATIONS`               | —        | Annotations JSON used for favorites or tag filters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `-o` `--output`          | `OUTPUT`                    | required | Where to write the reproduced CSV.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## check

`check` runs the **Data Management** page's **Data checks** on your tables without opening the app. It looks for:

- fixations lasting 0 ms or less, or with an infinite duration or onset;
- fixations and raw gaze samples with no finite position, or one more than a million pixels off the screen;
- word boxes with no area, or no finite position or size within a million pixels;
- screen sizes that are not finite and positive.

Each finding gives the rows and trials affected, a few example rows, and what the app does with them. `check` changes nothing and exits 0 whatever it finds. `--json` prints the table check_data_health returns. In example rows, missing values are `null` and infinite values are the strings `"Infinity"` or `"-Infinity"`. To save a QC record, use `--json-report`. Its `tables` object counts the source rows read, the rows with usable identifiers, and the normalized rows checked. Stimulus words shared across readings can expand into more checked rows. The report distinguishes empty tables, blank rows and rows with missing participant or trial IDs. Its `findings` list matches `--json`.

```
scanpath-studio check --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv
scanpath-studio check --raw-gaze gaze_samples.csv --json
```

| Option                   | Value                 | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------ | --------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--sample`               | switch                | —       | Check the bundled demo instead of your own tables.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--words`                | `PATH [PATH ...]`     | —       | Words table(s), as for render.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `--fixations`            | `PATH [PATH ...]`     | —       | Fixations table(s), as for render.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--raw-gaze`             | `PATH [PATH ...]`     | —       | The Raw gaze table, as for render.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--raw-gaze-schema`      | `JSON`                | —       | Column mapping for the `--raw-gaze` table, replacing auto-detection, in the form `--fix-schema` takes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--trial-parts-manifest` | `PATH`                | —       | JSON manifest assigning source rows to ordered screens.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `--json`                 | switch                | —       | Print the findings as JSON (the rows api.check_data_health returns).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--json-report`          | switch                | —       | Include input, eligible and checked row counts beside the findings as JSON.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `--word-schema`          | `JSON`                | —       | Column mapping for the `--words` table, replacing auto-detection. A JSON object from each field to a column name, or the path of a JSON file holding one, e.g. '{"trial": "TRIAL_INDEX", "word_id": "IA_ID", ...}'. It is the dict api.load_scanpath_data takes. Needed only when a column isn't recognized, and the error then prints a mapping to start from.     |
| `--fix-schema`           | `JSON`                | —       | Column mapping for the `--fixations` table, replacing auto-detection. A JSON object from each field to a column name, or the path of a JSON file holding one, e.g. '{"trial": "TRIAL_INDEX", "word_id": "IA_ID", ...}'. It is the dict api.load_scanpath_data takes. Needed only when a column isn't recognized, and the error then prints a mapping to start from. |
| `--keep-columns`         | `COLUMN [COLUMN ...]` | —       | More columns to keep through loading, under the names they have in your files (e.g. a pupil size), from whichever table has them. Without it, loading keeps only the mapped and recognized fields. A kept fixation column can be used by `--color-by`, an axis or a hover. Same as keep_columns= in api.load_scanpath_data.                                         |

## add

`add` adds your tables to the app's dataset list, as **Add dataset** does, without opening the app. Run `scanpath-studio` afterwards and the app opens on the new dataset. If the app is already open, reload its browser tab right away: changes you make in it before the reload are not saved. It works for an app on your own computer, not a hosted one.

```
scanpath-studio add "Pilot 3" --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv --canvas 1920x1080
scanpath-studio add "Pilot 3" --fixations fixations_v2.csv --replace
```

A name that is already saved is an error unless you pass `--replace`, which swaps the dataset's tables and keeps its annotations, metadata tables, share links, description and recording setup (unless you give a new description or `--canvas`). Without `--canvas`, the app uses a screen the data records, or estimates one from the extent of the data. In Python, use add_dataset.

**Positional arguments**

| Option | Value  | Default  | Description                      |
| ------ | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------- |
|        | `NAME` | required | The name the dataset list shows. |

**Options**

| Option                   | Value                 | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------ | --------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--words`                | `PATH [PATH ...]`     | —       | Words table(s), as for render.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `--fixations`            | `PATH [PATH ...]`     | —       | Fixations table(s), as for render.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--raw-gaze`             | `PATH [PATH ...]`     | —       | The Raw gaze table, as for render.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--raw-gaze-schema`      | `JSON`                | —       | Column mapping for the `--raw-gaze` table, replacing auto-detection, in the form `--fix-schema` takes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--trial-parts-manifest` | `PATH`                | —       | JSON manifest assigning source rows to ordered screens.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `--canvas`               | `WxH`                 | —       | The recording's screen in px, e.g. 1920x1080. Without it, a screen the data records is used, else one estimated from the extent of the data; with `--replace`, the saved dataset's setup is kept.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `--description`          | `TEXT`                | —       | The sentence the Data Management page shows under its name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `--replace`              | switch                | —       | Replace the tables of the saved dataset with this name, keeping its annotations, metadata tables, share links, and its description and recording setup unless `--description` or `--canvas` gives new ones. Without it, a name already saved is an error.                                                                                                           |
| `--no-select`            | switch                | —       | Add it to the list without opening the app on it next time.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `--word-schema`          | `JSON`                | —       | Column mapping for the `--words` table, replacing auto-detection. A JSON object from each field to a column name, or the path of a JSON file holding one, e.g. '{"trial": "TRIAL_INDEX", "word_id": "IA_ID", ...}'. It is the dict api.load_scanpath_data takes. Needed only when a column isn't recognized, and the error then prints a mapping to start from.     |
| `--fix-schema`           | `JSON`                | —       | Column mapping for the `--fixations` table, replacing auto-detection. A JSON object from each field to a column name, or the path of a JSON file holding one, e.g. '{"trial": "TRIAL_INDEX", "word_id": "IA_ID", ...}'. It is the dict api.load_scanpath_data takes. Needed only when a column isn't recognized, and the error then prints a mapping to start from. |
| `--keep-columns`         | `COLUMN [COLUMN ...]` | —       | More columns to keep through loading, under the names they have in your files (e.g. a pupil size), from whichever table has them. Without it, loading keeps only the mapped and recognized fields. A kept fixation column can be used by `--color-by`, an axis or a hover. Same as keep_columns= in api.load_scanpath_data.                                         |

## remove

`remove` takes a dataset you added, in the app or with `add`, off the app's dataset list. Its annotations, metadata tables and description go with it, as its **Remove** on the **Data Management** page does. Built-in and public datasets can't be removed. If the app last had it open, it next opens on its default dataset.

```
scanpath-studio remove "Pilot 3"
scanpath-studio remove "Pilot 3" --missing-ok   # no error if it isn't there
```

In Python, use remove_dataset.

**Positional arguments**

| Option | Value  | Default  | Description                                             |
| ------ | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
|        | `NAME` | required | The name the dataset list shows (case does not matter). |

**Options**

| Option         | Value  | Default | Description                                                          |
| -------------- | ------ | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--missing-ok` | switch | —       | Exit quietly when no dataset has the name, instead of with an error. |

## open

`open` opens the app on a dataset you added, or one the app has itself (the bundled demo, a public corpus), at one reading, with the figure set by the same flags [`render`](#render-flags) takes. If the app is running on this computer, the link opens in your browser. Otherwise `open` starts the app and opens the link once it is up. `--print` prints the link instead.

```
scanpath-studio open "Pilot 3" -p p07 -t t12
scanpath-studio open "Pilot 3" -p p07 -t t12 --heatmap --saccade-style dash --print
```

The link is the one **Share** → **Link** writes for the same view. Settings it leaves out keep the values the app has. It names the dataset, so a dataset you added opens only where it was added. A link carries no file: `render`'s input, output and `--stimulus-image` flags are refused, and `--show-stimulus-image` draws the dataset's own pages. In Python, use app_link.

**Positional arguments**

| Option | Value  | Default  | Description                           |
| ------ | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------- |
|        | `NAME` | required | The dataset's name in the app's list. |

**Options**

| Option               | Value         | Default | Description                                                    |
| -------------------- | ------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-p` `--participant` | `PARTICIPANT` | —       | Participant ID.                                                |
| `-t` `--trial`       | `TRIAL`       | —       | Trial ID (without it, the participant's first trial).          |
| `--screen`           | `SCREEN`      | —       | Screen ID within a trial recorded over several screens.        |
| `--animate`          | switch        | —       | Open the replay of the reading.                                |
| `--port`             | `PORT`        | `8501`  | The port the app listens on, or is started on (default: 8501). |
| `--print`            | switch        | —       | Print the link and exit, without opening or starting anything. |

## annotations

`annotations` reads and writes the favorites, tags and notes on a dataset you added. `export` writes the same `annotations.json` as **Data Management → Annotations → Export**, or a CSV table with one row per annotated reading. `import` reads either: a CSV needs `participant_id` and `trial_id`, optionally `screen_id`, and any of `favorite`, `tags` (separated by `;`, so a tag can't contain one in a CSV) and `note`. Importing adds a reading's tags to the ones it has, and a favorite or note in the file replaces its own; a blank stays as it was. This differs from the app's **Import**, which keeps or swaps a reading's whole entry. `--replace` makes the dataset's annotations exactly the file's, and is refused when none of the file's readings is in the dataset. Readings the dataset does not have are listed and left out. If the app is open, reload its browser tab to see the new ones.

```
scanpath-studio annotations import "Pilot 3" qc_flags.csv
scanpath-studio annotations export "Pilot 3" -o annotations.json
```

In Python, use write_annotations and read_annotations.

### annotations export

**Positional arguments**

| Option | Value  | Default  | Description                                             |
| ------ | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
|        | `NAME` | required | The name the dataset list shows (case does not matter). |

**Options**

| Option          | Value  | Default  | Description                       |
| --------------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-o` `--output` | `FILE` | required | The file to write, .json or .csv. |

### annotations import

**Positional arguments**

| Option | Value  | Default  | Description                                             |
| ------ | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
|        | `NAME` | required | The name the dataset list shows (case does not matter). |
|        | `FILE` | required | The .json or .csv file to read.                         |

**Options**

| Option      | Value  | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------- | ------ | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--replace` | switch | —       | Make the dataset's annotations exactly the file's, instead of adding the file's to them. Refused when none of the file's readings is in the dataset, so a file made for another dataset deletes nothing. |

## cache

A local or desktop run saves your session on your computer, so a refresh or a restart resumes where you left off. It saves uploaded datasets, column mappings, view settings, saved designs, metadata tables and annotations. `cache` shows what is stored and can delete it.

```
scanpath-studio cache            # datasets, rows, size, folder, last written
scanpath-studio cache --path     # just the folder
scanpath-studio cache --json     # the same status as JSON
scanpath-studio cache --clear    # delete the recovery cache
```

| Option    | Value  | Default | Description                      |
| --------- | ------ | ------- | -------------------------------- |
| `--path`  | switch | —       | Print the cache folder and exit. |
| `--json`  | switch | —       | Print the status as JSON.        |
| `--clear` | switch | —       | Delete the recovery cache.       |

Open **Data Management → Saved work → Your session** to see the same information. A running app writes a new copy at its next change, so clear the cache with the app closed.

| To                                       | Use                            |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| turn caching off for one launch          | `scanpath-studio --no-persist` |
| turn it off wherever the variable is set | `SCANPATH_STUDIO_PERSIST=0`    |
| move the folder                          | `SCANPATH_STUDIO_STATE_DIR`    |

Hosted deployments do not cache by default.

## version

`version` says which build this is and how it was installed. `--check` also asks GitHub whether a newer release is out and says how to update your install. Only `--check` uses the network.

```
scanpath-studio version           # the build, and how it was installed
scanpath-studio version --check   # …and whether a newer release is out
```

| Option      | Value     | Default | Description                                                           |
| ----------- | --------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--check`   | switch    | —       | Ask GitHub for the latest release and say how to update this install. |
| `--timeout` | `SECONDS` | `5.0`   | How long to wait for GitHub, in seconds (default: 5).                 |

Between releases the version names the build: `0.35.0.post3+g8f18219` is three commits after 0.35.0, at commit `8f18219`. In a local install or the desktop app, open **Help → About & citation → App details → :material:update: Check for updates**. In Python, call check_for_updates.

## cite

`cite` prints how to cite Scanpath Studio. `--corpus` adds the citation of the public corpus you used.

```
scanpath-studio cite                           # BibTeX
scanpath-studio cite --format apa --corpus onestop
scanpath-studio cite --format credit           # one sentence for a figure caption
```

| Option     | Value                                        | Default  | Description                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--format` | `bibtex`, `apa`, `ris`, `csl-json`, `credit` | `bibtex` | Bibtex (default), apa, ris (Zotero, Mendeley, EndNote), csl-json, or credit: one sentence to paste into a figure caption. |
| `--corpus` | `onestop`, `potec`                           | —        | Add this public corpus's citation after the software's.                                                                   |

You don't have to add the citation to your files by hand: every figure `render` writes carries it in its file metadata. The same entries are cite in Python.

# Across the experiment

Mean total fixation duration per paragraph word across one participant’s trials in the bundled demo. Each point is one trial. The bundled demo holds only part of the session.

1. Open your data in the **Corpus Analysis** view and select **Participants**.
1. Choose a participant and select **Open participant profile**. In **Chart settings**, set **View** to **Per-trial trend**.
1. Choose a reading measure your data provides, and **Mean** in **Aggregate**. The horizontal axis is the trial order from the data’s `trial_index` or `TRIAL_INDEX` column. Without one, the app orders the trials by fixation time, or as listed.

[Follow the progression tutorial](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/tutorials/corpus-analysis/progression-over-time/index.md)

The corpus CLI does not offer trial-order trends. Download the [Python recipe](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/gallery/across-experiment/across-experiment.py) and run:

```
python across-experiment.py
```

This uses the app’s aggregation and trend builder.

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

from scanpath_studio.aggregation import metric_by_trial_index
from scanpath_studio.data import derive_trial_index
from scanpath_studio.plots import make_trend_figure

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data(names="canonical")
reader = words[
    (words["participant_id"] == "l37_273") & (words["screen_id"] == "Paragraph")
].copy()
reader["trial_index"] = derive_trial_index(reader)
trend = metric_by_trial_index(reader, "total_fixation_duration_ms")
fig = make_trend_figure(
    trend,
    x_col="trial_index",
    x_label="Recorded trial order",
    y_label="Mean total fixation duration per word (ms)",
    title="Across the experiment · Participant A",
    canvas_width=1000,
    base_font_size=18,
    font_family="Arial",
    height=450,
    break_gaps=True,
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "across-experiment.html")
```

[← All examples](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/gallery/index.md)

# Two participants

Two complete readings of a shorter text, labeled Participant A and Participant B.

1. Open your data in the **Scanpath View** and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. Turn on **Compare**. In **Trial B**, choose another participant's reading of the same text.
1. In **Compare settings**, set **Layout** to **Overlay** and name the two readings under **Reading labels**. To compare the complete readings, keep the **Index range** of both scanpaths at the full range, under **Filters & highlights** ▾ → **Reading A** and **Reading B**.
1. In **Figure** → **Screen & framing**, tick **Crop to data**. Under **Margins and border color**, untick the automatic margin and enter 50 px.
1. Under **Legends** → **Legend position and style**, set **Compare (A/B)** to **Top center, outside** and **Side by side**, with text size 24.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio-dev.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_273 -t l37_273_2_2_4_Ele --screen Paragraph \
  --compare-with l7_183:l7_183_2_2_4_Ele --compare-screen Paragraph \
  --compare-legend --label-a "Participant A" --label-b "Participant B" \
  --legend compare=top-center-outside,side-by-side,24 \
  --crop-to-data --crop-margin 50 \
  --highlight-column '' \
  -o comparison.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
pid, tid = "l37_273", "l37_273_2_2_4_Ele"
fig = sps.compare_scanpaths(
    words,
    fixations,
    (pid, tid),
    ("l7_183", "l7_183_2_2_4_Ele"),
    screen="Paragraph",
    screen_b="Paragraph",
    labels=("Participant A", "Participant B"),
    fit_to_monitor=False,
    crop_margin=50,
    show_legend=True,
    duration_size_legend=False,
    legend_layout={
        "compare": {
            "position": "top-center-outside",
            "arrangement": "side-by-side",
            "size": 24,
        }
    },
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "comparison.html")
```

[← All examples](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/gallery/index.md)

# Fully customizable

Make a figure for a talk or teaching: pink hearts for fixations, purple arrows for the eye’s movements. This hand-drawn illustration follows The → cat → sat → on → the → mat, with one fixation per word.

1. Load your Words and Fixations tables, or the example [words](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/gallery/hearts-arrows/words.csv) and [fixations](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/gallery/hearts-arrows/fixations.csv). For the example, set **Recording setup** → **Screen** to **I know it**, 450 × 300 px. Open the dataset in the **Scanpath View** and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. In **Fixations** → **Marker appearance**, set **Shape** to **♥ Heart**. Keep **Color** at **One color** and set its box to `#d12d72`. Set **Size** to **18–30** and **Opacity** to **0.85**. Under **Position on the text**, tick **Snap to line**, and leave **Fixation index** → **Show** unticked.
1. In **Saccades** → **Line and arrow appearance**, set **Shape** to **Arc**. In the main Saccades menu, keep **Color** at **One color** with `#4f46a5`, and set **Width** to **2.5**. Tick **Direction arrows** and set **Line and arrow appearance** → **Arrow size** to **12**.
1. In **Figure** → **Title & labels** → **Illustration**, enter “Illustration · hand-drawn” in **Text**. Leave **Stimulus** ▾ → **Highlight words** unticked.

Save the look under **My views** to apply it to your own data.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio-dev.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

Download the example [words](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/gallery/hearts-arrows/words.csv) and [fixations](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/gallery/hearts-arrows/fixations.csv) into the same folder.

```
scanpath-studio render --words words.csv --fixations fixations.csv \
  -p synthetic -t synthetic_2line_demo --canvas 450x300 \
  --fixation-symbol heart --fixation-color '#d12d72' \
  --marker-size-range 18 30 --fixation-opacity 0.85 --snap-fixations \
  --saccade-arcs --saccade-arrows --saccade-color '#4f46a5' \
  --saccade-width 2.5 --saccade-arrow-size 12 \
  --no-fixation-index --highlight-column '' \
  --illustration-text "Illustration · hand-drawn" -o hearts-arrows.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

from scanpath_studio.synthetic import make_synthetic_words

words = make_synthetic_words()
fixations = words[["participant_id", "trial_id", "text_id", "word_id"]].copy()
fixations["x"] = words["x"] + words["width"] / 2
fixations["y"] = words["y"] + words["height"] / 2
fixations["duration_ms"] = [100, 150, 120, 200, 90, 110]
fixations["timestamp_ms"] = (
    fixations["duration_ms"].cumsum() - fixations["duration_ms"]
)
fixations["order_in_trial"] = range(1, len(fixations) + 1)
fixations["pass_index"] = 1
pid, tid = "synthetic", "synthetic_2line_demo"
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(
    words,
    fixations,
    pid,
    tid,
    canvas_size=(450, 300),
    fixation_symbol="heart",
    fixation_color="#d12d72",
    marker_size_range=(18, 30),
    fixation_opacity=0.85,
    fixation_snap_to_line=True,
    saccade_render_mode="Arc",
    show_saccade_arrows=True,
    saccade_color="#4f46a5",
    saccade_width=2.5,
    saccade_arrow_size=12,
    show_order=False,
    duration_size_legend=False,
    illustration_text="Illustration · hand-drawn",
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "hearts-arrows.html")
```

[← All examples](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/gallery/index.md)

# Heatmap

Where fixation time concentrates.

1. Open your data in the **Scanpath View** and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. Turn on **Heatmap**. In **Heatmap** ▾ → **Style**, choose **Smoothed**. Keep **Color** → **By** at **Duration (ms)**.
1. Turn off **Fixations** and **Saccades**, and keep **Stimulus** on.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio-dev.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_273 -t l37_273_2_1_1_Ele --screen Paragraph \
  --heatmap --heatmap-style smoothed --no-fixations --no-saccades \
  --highlight-column '' \
  -o heatmap.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
pid, tid = "l37_273", "l37_273_2_1_1_Ele"
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(
    words,
    fixations,
    pid,
    tid,
    screen="Paragraph",
    show_heatmap=True,
    heatmap_style="Smoothed",
    show_fixations=False,
    show_saccades=False,
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "heatmap.html")
```

[← All examples](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/gallery/index.md)

# Highlighted text

Highlight a selected text span alongside its fixations.

1. Load a Words table with a true/false column that marks the words to highlight, and your Fixations table. Open the dataset in the **Scanpath View** and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. In **Stimulus** ▾, tick **Highlight words** and choose that column.
1. Under **Style**, keep **Mark text** and pick the highlight color in the box beside it. To show only the highlighted text and the fixations, turn off **Saccades**.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio-dev.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
  --highlight-column is_in_aspan --critical-span-style mark-text \
  --no-saccades -o highlighted-text.html
```


# Reading schematic

A hand-drawn two-line text, with one fixation per word in reading order: The → cat → sat → on → the → mat. Fixations sit on the lines and saccades are arcs.

1. Load your Words and Fixations tables, or the example [words](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/gallery/illustration/words.csv) and [fixations](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/gallery/illustration/fixations.csv). For the example, set **Recording setup** → **Screen** to **I know it**, 450 × 340 px.
1. Open the dataset in the **Scanpath View** and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. In **Fixations** ▾, open **Position on the text** and tick **Snap to line** and **Fixation index** → **Show**. In **Saccades** → **Line and arrow appearance** → **Shape**, choose **Arc**.
1. In **Figure** → **Title & labels** → **Illustration**, enter “Illustration · hand-drawn” in **Text**.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio-dev.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
scanpath-studio render --words words.csv --fixations fixations.csv \
  -p synthetic -t synthetic_2line_demo \
  --canvas 450x340 --snap-fixations --saccade-arcs --fixation-index \
  --illustration-text "Illustration · hand-drawn" \
  --highlight-column '' -o illustration.html
```

```

fixations["x"] = words["x"] + words["width"] / 2
fixations["y"] = words["y"] + words["height"] / 2
fixations["duration_ms"] = [100, 150, 120, 200, 90, 110]
fixations["timestamp_ms"] = (
    fixations["duration_ms"].cumsum() - fixations["duration_ms"]
)
fixations["order_in_trial"] = range(1, len(fixations) + 1)
fixations["pass_index"] = 1

    words,
    fixations,
    pid,
    tid,
    canvas_size=(450, 340),
```

# Redacted text

Show where the text was without showing what it said. Each word is drawn as a rounded block over its letters. Words are also hidden in tooltips.

1. Open your data in the **Scanpath View** and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. In **Stimulus** ▾ → **Text**, tick **Redact**. The blocks take the text color.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio-dev.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_273 -t l37_273_2_1_1_Ele --screen Paragraph \
  --redact-text --highlight-column '' \
  -o redacted-text.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
pid, tid = "l37_273", "l37_273_2_1_1_Ele"
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(
    words, fixations, pid, tid, screen="Paragraph", redact_text=True
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "redacted-text.html")
```

[← All examples](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/gallery/index.md)

# Replay

Replay a reading in fixation order. Press **▶ Play** above the text to start this example, **⏸ Pause** to stop, or drag the time slider to inspect a moment. The example shows the first forty fixations at twice the recorded speed.

1. Open your data in the **Scanpath View** and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. Choose **Animation**. To replay part of the reading, set **Filters & highlights** ▾ → **Fixations** → **Index range**, here 1 to 40.
1. In **Animation settings** → **Replay** → **Speed**, choose **×2**, then press **▶ Play** above the plot. Use **⏸ Pause** or the time slider to inspect the reading.
1. Save the replay from **Export** → **Current figure**.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio-dev.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_273 -t l37_273_2_1_1_Ele --screen Paragraph \
  --animate --fix-index-range 1:40 --playback-speed 2 \
  --highlight-column '' \
  -o replay.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
pid, tid = "l37_273", "l37_273_2_1_1_Ele"
fig = sps.animate_scanpath(
    words,
    fixations,
    pid,
    tid,
    screen="Paragraph",
    fix_index_range=(1, 40),
    playback_speed=2.0,
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "replay.html")
```

[← All examples](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/gallery/index.md)

# Saccade types

# Scanpath

Fixations and saccades over the text.

1. Save the figure from **Export** → **Current figure**.

# Fixations by line

Fixations colored by their nearest text line.

1. Open your data in the **Scanpath View** and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. In **Fixations** → **Color**, choose **Text line (computed)**.
1. Keep **Saccades** and **Stimulus** on. Each fixation takes the color of the nearest line of word boxes.

# Title, caption & legend

A figure ready for a slide or a paper. It has a title above the plot, a caption below it, the **Saccade types** legend down the right side and the **Fixation sizes** legend below the plot.

1. Open your data in the **Scanpath View** and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. In **Saccades** → **Color**, choose **By type**.
1. In **Figure** → **Title & labels**, tick **Title** and **Caption**. Enter a title for your reading and a caption that explains the markers and colors. Under **Text size and color**, set each size, here 34 px and 20 px.
1. Under **Legends**, tick **Show** for **Fixation sizes**. Open **Legend position and style** and set **Saccade types** to **Right, outside** and **Fixation sizes** to **Bottom right, outside**, both with text size 18.
1. Under **Screen & framing**, tick **Crop to data**. Under **Margins and border color**, untick the automatic margin and enter 60 px.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio-dev.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_273 -t l37_273_2_1_1_Ele --screen Paragraph \
  --saccade-color-by-type \
  --title "One participant, one article" --title-size 34 \
  --caption "Marker size: fixation duration. Line color: saccade type." --caption-size 20 \
  --duration-size-legend --legend saccades=right-outside,,18 --legend size-key=bottom-right-outside,,18 \
  --crop-to-data --crop-margin 60 \
  --highlight-column '' \
  -o title-caption-legend.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
pid, tid = "l37_273", "l37_273_2_1_1_Ele"
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(
    words,
    fixations,
    pid,
    tid,
    screen="Paragraph",
    saccade_color_mode="By type",
    title="One participant, one article",
    title_font_size=34,
    caption="Marker size: fixation duration. Line color: saccade type.",
    caption_font_size=20,
    duration_size_legend=True,
    legend_layout={
        "saccades": {"position": "right-outside", "size": 18},
        "size_key": {"position": "bottom-right-outside", "size": 18},
    },
    fit_to_monitor=False,
    crop_margin=60,
)

sps.save_figure(fig, "title-caption-legend.html")
```

[← All examples](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/gallery/index.md)

# Word-box heatmap

Fixation time within each word box.

1. Open your data in the **Scanpath View** and pick a trial in **Select trial**.
1. Turn on **Heatmap**. In **Heatmap** ▾ → **Style**, choose **Word boxes**. Keep **Color** → **By** at **Duration (ms)**.
1. Turn off **Fixations** and **Saccades**, and keep **Stimulus** on.

[Open the demo](https://scanpath-studio-dev.streamlit.app) · [All controls](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/guides/scanpath-visualization/controls/index.md)

```
scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_273 -t l37_273_2_1_1_Ele --screen Paragraph \
  --heatmap --heatmap-style word-boxes --no-fixations --no-saccades \
  --highlight-column '' \
  -o word-boxes.html
```

```
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
pid, tid = "l37_273", "l37_273_2_1_1_Ele"
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(
    words,
    fixations,
    pid,
    tid,
    screen="Paragraph",
    show_heatmap=True,
    heatmap_style="Word boxes",

    show_saccades=False,
)

```

# About

# About Scanpath Studio

Scanpath Studio visualizes eye movements in reading. **Help** opens the documentation for your Stable or Dev build. **About & citation → App details** links to [what’s new in that build](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/dev/whats-new/index.md).

Developed by [Omer Shubi](https://omershubi.github.io/), [Maya Grossman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/maya-grossman-32b547292/), [Keren Gruteke Klein](https://kerengruteke.github.io/), [Deborah N. Jakobi](https://www.cl.uzh.ch/en/research-groups/digital-linguistics/people/lab-members/jakobi.html), [Ella Lion](https://ella-lion.github.io/), [Carlson Büth](https://www.cl.uzh.ch/en/research-groups/digital-linguistics/people/lab-members/bueth.html), [David R. Reich](https://www.cl.uzh.ch/en/research-groups/digital-linguistics/people/lab-members/reich.html), [Lena Jäger](https://www.cl.uzh.ch/en/research-groups/digital-linguistics/people/group-leader/jaeger.html), and [Yevgeni Berzak](https://dds.technion.ac.il/people/academic-staff/yevgeni-berzak/), at the Technion and the University of Zurich.

## Cite Scanpath Studio

Cite the software using its [Zenodo DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22933884). In the app, **Help** → **About & citation** → **Citation** gives the APA reference and a copyable BibTeX entry. Use `scanpath-studio cite` in a terminal or cite in Python to get the citation. Both also offer RIS and CSL-JSON formats.
